notes: τῶν εἰδωλοθύτων splits under rule 102: the article takes the supplied nominal things and the adjective takes sacrificed to idols. Reading things as the adjective's own generic completion under rule 17 with the article unrepresented remains defensible, but rule 17's generic-noun clause is scoped by rule 102 to anarthrous Greek and an article stands here.
Both articles standing before γνῶσις and ἀγάπη are unrepresented under rule 23: the ASV writes those nouns with no determiner of any kind, so nothing of rules 19, 51 or 60 is in question.
ὅτι is aligned to the supplied that (rule 43); the clause is reported and the ASV writes the complementizer, so no unrepresented reading arises.
πάντες keeps a bare all and the supplied subject we rides with ἔχομεν discontinuously under rule 15, the person of the verb being what licenses it (rule 9).
